**The question bug is fixed** (#207254, `fc89603`, in the lander's queue).
- **Cause:** answering one question I'd asked you closed every other open question from me, and typing anything in my conversation closed them too.
- **Now:** only an answer to that specific question closes it (its card or a Reply).
- **One change in behaviour:** typing "yes" in the composer no longer closes a question.
- The fix is about −70 lines net.

**The open-questions place.** This is an assessment; nothing is built. It's small to medium, about +250 / −40 lines.
- **Questions tab:** a new tab in the right panel lists every open question to you. Each has its answer card plus a **Dismiss** button.
- **Top bar:** the "N waiting on you" count opens that tab from anywhere.
- **My side:** each turn starts with a line listing what's still open to you and how long ago I asked, and I treat those as unanswered.
- **Dismiss:** a dismissal reaches me as a note.
- **Easier alternative:** about +60 lines. It adds only a Dismiss button on the inline card, makes the count jump to the oldest open question, and adds my prompt line, so you lose the side-by-side list.

Decisions (my picks are 1a, 2a, 3a, go):
1. **Where open questions live:** (a) the Questions tab, opened from the top-bar count; (b) the easier version.
2. **Questions I ask in a final answer** (like the system-prompt one at the end of my last answer): (a) I always ask through a real question message, so every question is in one list, and the cards that close when you type go away; (b) keep those cards, but add Dismiss and stop typing from closing them.
3. **A dismissal:** (a) reaches me as a note for my next turn; (b) wakes me right away.

Still open from my last answer: should I start a small coordinator to take the live conversation list out of my system prompt? That's the "system prompt · 1 section" dividers, and it would save prompt-cache tokens.

**Landed: the question bug fix** (`fc89603`, #207254), pushed.
- Only an answer to a specific question closes it: its card, or a Reply to that message.
- Answering one question leaves your other open questions open.
- Typing in the composer no longer closes any question.

**Started:** #208357 is assessing the "system prompt · 1 section" dividers. It finds which prompt sections change every turn, measures what that costs in prompt cache, and proposes how to stop it.

Your earlier answer may have closed the open-questions decisions before the fix landed, so here they are again. My picks are 1a, 2a, 3a, go:

1. **Where open questions live:** (a) a Questions tab in the right panel, opened from the top-bar "waiting on you" count, each question with its answer card and a Dismiss button; (b) the easier version: only a Dismiss button on the inline card, and the count jumps to the oldest open question.
2. **Questions I ask at the end of a final answer:** (a) I always ask through a real question message, so every question sits in one list; (b) keep those cards, but add Dismiss and stop typing from closing them.
3. **A dismissal:** (a) reaches me as a note for my next turn; (b) wakes me right away.

Reply e.g. "1a 2a 3a, go".

**The "system prompt · 1 section" dividers cost real money** (#208357). It's an assessment; nothing is built yet.

**What changes:** my system prompt changed 387 times in two days.
- **Conversations list:** 342 of those changes come from the list of other conversations, rebuilt on every branch start, conclude and retitle.
- **Hot reloads:** 81 (`build`).
- **Switching between Agent and System:** 43 (`surface`).

**Cost:** on the Claude Code path, a changed system prompt throws away the prompt cache 74% of the time. A turn after a change costs about **$1.30**, against $0.09 without one. Over two days that's up to about **$185 of my ~$390**. It's an upper bound, since some of those turns would have missed the cache anyway after idle gaps, but most of it is real.

**Fix:** small, about −60 / +10 lines.
- **The conversations section** keeps only its warning ("others may share your checkout; check `git status`…") and drops the list. I read the list when I need it with `ultimate.conversations()`, as I already do.
- **The `surface` section** (which tab you're looking at) is deleted.
- **`build`** stays, because hot-swap awareness matters and those are real code changes.
- **What you see:** dividers almost disappear, and my turns get cheaper and faster.

**Easier alternative:** only hide those dividers (about 5 lines). That fixes the noise but keeps the cost.

Decisions (my picks are 1a, 2a, 3a, 4b, go):
1. **Conversations list:** (a) fixed text with no list; (b) keep the list with ids and folders only (fewer changes, but branch starts and concludes still break the cache).
2. **`surface`:** (a) delete it; (b) turn it into a per-message note.
3. **The open-questions line #207254 is building:** (a) a per-message note, so asking or answering doesn't break the cache. I've already told #207254 to build it that way, pending your confirmation. (b) A system-prompt section.
4. **Also hide dividers for `build`:** (a) yes; (b) no, they're meaningful now.
5. Build it?

Reply e.g. "1a 2a 3a 4b, go".

**A Review surface** (#209732): an assessment; nothing is built yet.

**Verdict:** medium, about 900–1,200 new lines, all in a new `extensions/review/`, with one new dependency: `@pierre/diffs`, the library DiffsHub is built on (Apache-2.0).

**How it would work:**
- **Diffs come from local git, not GitHub.** It works for private repos like poe2-rust, uncommitted changes and offline. It shows a branch vs main, a landing range, a single commit, or what's uncommitted.
- **The library** handles the diff, line selection, comments and virtualization. It reuses the syntax highlighter we already ship, only loads when you open Review, and is restyled to our theme.
- **A plain file list** instead of their file tree: theirs is a beta that bundles another React-like library.
- **Commenting:** select lines, write a comment, collect several, then press "Send review (3)". It arrives as your own input in the branch that made the change (a landing goes to whoever submitted it), otherwise to me; a picker can change the recipient. The recipient gets a "Review · 3 comments" card with each file:line, the code excerpt and your comment, and it wakes.
- **Links:** `/?review=<range>` opens it. The "N commits" counts on landing cards and in the Activity feed open Review, the DiffsHub link stays as the external one, and branch rows get "Review changes".
- **Built in two rounds**, each with a preview for you: the viewer and links first, then comments and sending.

**Easier alternative:** keep the DiffsHub links (#209751 is doing that now) and add a "comment on this range" box, about 150 lines. You lose private repos, uncommitted changes, offline use and selecting code to send.

**Risks:**
- Huge diffs (lockfiles) can be slow, so files collapse by default and there's a size cap per file.
- The library moves fast, so it's pinned exactly.
- One small extra copy of a diff library.

Decisions (my picks are 1a, 2a, 3a, 4a, 5a, go):
1. **Approach:** (a) the full Review surface; (b) only DiffsHub links plus a comment box.
2. **File list:** (a) a plain list; (b) their file tree.
3. **How reviews arrive:** (a) as your input with a review card; (b) as a message from you, which would bring back user-sent messages, removed in the cleanup.
4. **Default recipient:** (a) the branch or landing submitter, otherwise me; (b) always me.
5. **First version:** (a) all four range kinds; (b) only landings and branches first.

Reply e.g. "1a 2a 3a 4a 5a, go".

**The stable prompt is working** (#208357). Since the switch there's been no more cache miss from the conversation list or the tab line. Before the fix there were 15 of those in 30 minutes, each about $2.

**What still causes misses:** the `build` line in my prompt changes on every hot reload. That's about every 10 minutes on a busy landing day, or 81 of the 387 prompt changes so far, and each costs a full cache rewrite (about $2.20 at today's context size). The fix is to move the build line out of the system prompt and tell me in a short note on my next input when the build changed. I'd keep the same awareness of hot swaps without the cache cost. It's small.

**Landed: `pnpm reset`** (`5ef0c6e`, #206639).
- **What it does:** moves the conversation state into `~/.ultimate/backups/reset-<time>/`.
- **What stays:** settings, secrets, logins, worktrees and branches.
- **Safety:** it lists unlanded work, refuses while Ultimate runs, and has `--dry-run`.
- **After a reset:** start Ultimate and click **Move here** once. That takes the project back with the fresh state, without downloading the old one.
- **Where the old history lives:** only in the backup folder and in older cloud backups, until those are pruned.
- **Restart:** it changes `server/harness.ts`, so the guard that refuses to start on a half-finished reset only applies after a host restart. The script itself works already.

Decisions:
1. **Phase words** (still open): (a) keep them; (b) remove the phase extension entirely.
2. **The build line:** (a) move it to a per-input note when it changes (recommended); (b) leave it.
3. **Host restart for `pnpm reset`'s start guard:** (a) restart now; it takes a few seconds and running conversations resume (recommended); (b) later.

Reply e.g. "1b 2a 3a".

**Your own actions in the system log: partly.** I checked the trace and events.

**Captured today:**
- **Every server call the UI makes**, traced with caller `ui` and the conversation: for example your answer card just now (`questions/answer`), plus the reads behind panels you open (`secrets/list`, `lineage/recent`, `instance/list`). Repeated polls are counted, not stored, so only one-off actions show as rows.
- **Your answers to my questions:** a `board.sent` event from `user`, e.g. message 1164, your "Yes".

**Not captured:**
- **Prompts you type:** they're entries in the conversation's transcript, but there's no event for them, so the System stream doesn't show "user sent a prompt / steered / queued a follow-up".
- **Navigation:** switching surfaces (Agent, System, Review), opening a conversation, opening a panel or tab. These happen only in the browser and never reach the server.
- **Which device or tab** an action came from.

**Proposal, without going overboard:** three things, all small, extensions only, no restart.
1. **`user.input`:** emitted server-side in the same commit as the input, with the conversation, kind (prompt, steer, follow-up, answer, dismiss), its entry id and length. No text: the transcript already holds it, and the entry id links to it.
2. **`ui.navigated`:** the browser reports only real changes of surface or open conversation, through one tiny action, debounced. No clicks, hovers or scrolls.
3. **Device:** each of these events carries a short device label (desktop or phone, browser) and your Tailscale login when the request came through Tailscale.

Your actions then line up with the agents' work in the System stream, e.g. "you opened Review → sent a review → #209732 woke".

Two decisions:
1. **User actions in the log:** (a) all three (recommended); (b) only `user.input`; (c) not now.
2. **The `secrets/list` bursts from my last answer:** (a) fix them: a one-line change so the list is only re-read when an extension is enabled, disabled or changes which secrets it declares, not on every hot reload (recommended); (b) leave it.

Reply e.g. "1a 2a".

**An updater for Ultimate** (#221387): an assessment; nothing is built yet. It's medium, about +400 / −40 lines: one small new extension, plus moving the existing fast-forward code into a shared helper. Nothing in `server/` or `bin/` changes.

**What it found:**
- **Most of it exists already:** the fetch with its SSH/HTTPS fallback, the fast-forward with its refusals, and the "core changed · restart" item, which already appears after a pull that touches `server/`.
- **A real gap:** moves fast-forward the *project* checkout, never the Ultimate clone. So on a machine where Ultimate runs a different project, like poe2-rust on haza-pc, the clone never updates today.

**The recommended design:**
- **Checking:** every running Ultimate checks its clone, but at most one real `git fetch` per clone per hour, plus once at startup; git's own `FETCH_HEAD` timestamp is shared, so several projects on one clone don't each fetch. Counting the new commits is local and free.
- **Status line:** shows `↓ 5 new` only when the clone is behind. Its popover lists the commit subjects, a DiffsHub link for the range, and what they touch (extensions/web reload by themselves, server ⚠, lockfile ⚠). Buttons: **Later** and **Update now**.
- **Update now:** fast-forward, `pnpm install` if the lockfile changed, then a short report: what reloaded by itself, where "core changed · restart" now appears, and a note if `bin/` changed.
- **Refusals:** a dirty clone, another branch or a diverged branch get a message and an **Ask @sync** link. It never stashes, rebases or resets.
- **ROG:** this clone is also the project, and landings keep it current, so normally nothing shows. Updates are refused while the lander is landing.
- **Events:** `update.applied` and `update.refused` appear in the System stream and in @sync's feedback.

**Easier alternative:** about 80 lines. Only the `↓ 5 new` badge with the commit list and a "copy command" button for `git pull --ff-only && pnpm install`. No one-click update and no refusal messages.

Decisions (my picks are 1a, 2a, 3a, 4a, 5a, go):
1. **Scope:** (a) the full flow with the Update button; (b) badge plus copy command only.
2. **Restart after a core change:** (a) you click "core changed · restart" in each running Ultimate; (b) it restarts by itself once that instance is idle.
3. **Interval:** (a) hourly plus at startup; (b) every 30 min.
4. **ROG:** (a) refuse only while the lander is landing; (b) never update a clone that is also a project, badge only.
5. **@sync's role:** (a) only an "Ask @sync" link when an update is refused, plus the events; (b) @sync runs every update.

Reply e.g. "1a 2a 3a 4a 5a, go".

**Why boxer went to standby on sentry-mac:** idle release. The setting `cloud.idleRelease` defaults to **10 minutes**. When a project has run nothing for that long (no conversation, no lander run, no automation due), its machine uploads a snapshot, frees the lease and goes to "Released · resume here". ROG never does this because its settings have `cloud.idleRelease: 0`; the Mac uses the default. Your card shows exactly that: on start, sentry-mac claimed boxer automatically (epoch 5), then released it after 10 idle minutes.

**Why boxer isn't on the fleet page:** the page lists only projects with a running writer, as we decided during the cloud cleanup. A released project has no writer, so it's hidden, even though sentry-mac itself is up and serving the standby page.

**My take:** idle release made sense when the cloud held a copy and you could open a project anywhere. Now that you connect over Tailscale to whichever machine runs a project, releasing it only makes it unreachable until you click Resume. It also doubled as a backup, but **Back up now** covers that.

**Unblock now:** on the Mac, set `"idleRelease": 0` under `cloud` in `~/.ultimate/settings.json`, restart Ultimate there, and click **Resume here**.

Decisions (my picks are 1a, 2a, go):
1. **Idle release:** (a) delete it. A machine keeps a project until a move or a clean stop, and the setting goes away. (b) Keep it, but default to 0 (never). (c) Leave it as is.
2. **Fleet page:** (a) also list projects that are free or on standby, quietly: "boxer · free · last on sentry-mac", with **Open on tailnet** going to that machine's standby page, where **Resume here** is. (b) Keep showing only running projects.

**Setup health** (#222679): an assessment; nothing is built yet.

**The Mac's summarizer, confirmed:** boxer's default summary model is `openai-codex/gpt-6-luna`, and sentry-mac has no openai-codex login, so the code just skips every summary feature without saying so. Boxer's trace shows 10 summary-model lookups, all empty, and not one summary call since this morning. That turns off codemode lines, titles, reply summaries and question extraction. It also means message triage doesn't run, so every message wakes boxer's @ultimate. The phase words do work there; they use a different service.

**Recommendation:** medium, about +350 / −60 lines, extensions only, no restart.
- **Summary model falls back:** if the configured model has no login, use a good cheap model you do have (on the Mac, an openrouter one) and show a notice once. Only when the setting is the default; if you chose one yourself, it warns instead of overriding you.
- **Setup check in the status line:** "⚠ 2 setup issues", shown only when something needs attention. Its popover lists:
  - the summary model and its fallback;
  - agents pinned to a provider with no login. On the Mac, the lander and the reviewers use openai-codex, so landing and review will fail there.
  - failing providers, missing secrets (absorbing today's "N secrets missing" item), half-set-up cloud, extensions that failed to load, and no lander checks.

  Each row has a fix link: Secrets panel, provider login, Ask @sync.
- **My side:** a one-line note on my next input whenever the set of issues changes, so I can tell you what's missing.
- **Cost:** checks only read files and state, no model calls.

**Easier alternative:** only the summary-model fallback, about 40 lines. It fixes what you hit today, but the lander and reviewer problem on the Mac stays invisible until a landing fails.

**Decisions** (my picks: 1a 2a 3a 4a 5a, go):
1. **Scope:** (a) fallback + setup check + my note; (b) fallback only; (c) check only, no fallback.
2. **Fallback pick:** (a) first available from a short list of known-good cheap models, then the cheapest; (b) always the cheapest.
3. **A summary model you set yourself but can't use:** (a) warn only; (b) fall back too.
4. **"N secrets missing":** (a) fold into the setup item; (b) keep both.
5. **My note when setup changes:** (a) yes, only when the issues change; (b) no, status line only.

Reply e.g. "1a 2a 3a 4a 5a, go".

**Why boxer sleeps on the Mac and ultimate doesn't here:** it's the idle-release setting, `cloud.idleRelease`.
- **Default, 10 minutes:** when a project runs nothing for 10 minutes (no conversation, no lander run, no automation due), its machine uploads a snapshot, frees the project and shows "Released · resume here". The Mac uses this default.
- **ROG:** `~/.ultimate/settings.json` here has `"idleRelease": 0` (never). We set that on 2026-10-18 so ROG would keep the project.

Since boxer is released, it also disappears from the fleet page, which only lists projects with a running machine.

**Fix it on the Mac now:** add `"idleRelease": 0` under `cloud` in its `~/.ultimate/settings.json`, restart Ultimate there, and click **Resume here** once.

**For good** (my picks are 1a, 2a): idle release made sense when the cloud held a copy you could open anywhere. Now you connect over Tailscale to whichever machine runs a project, so releasing it only makes it unreachable until you click Resume, and **Back up now** covers the backup side.

1. **Idle release:** (a) delete it: a machine keeps a project until you move it or stop Ultimate cleanly; (b) keep it, but default to 0 (never); (c) leave it as is.
2. **Fleet page:** (a) also list released projects quietly, e.g. "boxer · free · last on sentry-mac", linking to that machine's page with **Resume here**; (b) keep listing only running projects.

Reply e.g. "1a 2a".

**Worktree setup** (#226722): an assessment; nothing is built yet.

**The "prepare workspace" step already exists.** Every worktree (coordinators, workers, the lander) runs the project's `isolates.worktree.setup` before its first tool call; a failure blocks tools and retries. Boxer already has one: `composer install`, `npm ci`, a fresh `.env` and Wayfinder, about 20 s.

**What's missing:** setup gets no worktree id or port, nothing it sets reaches later commands, nothing runs when a worktree is removed, and every command is capped at 120 s. A fresh boxer worktree still has no database, and its dev server collides with the main checkout on :8000 and :5173.

**Recommendation:** small to medium, about +150 lines, extensions only, no restart. Ultimate gives the hook, ports and environment; the database work stays in each project's own script.
- **Ports:** each worktree reserves a block of 10 ports from 20000 up, recorded so they never collide and freed when it's removed.
- **Environment:** setup and every command in that worktree get `ULTIMATE_PORT`, `ULTIMATE_WORKTREE`, `ULTIMATE_CONVERSATION` and `ULTIMATE_SOURCE`, plus `ULTIMATE_LANDER=1` in the lander's checkout so it can skip the database. Only ports and paths, never secrets.
- **Teardown:** new `isolates.worktree.teardown` commands run before a finished worktree is removed, to stop its dev server and drop its database. A failure is only a notice.
- **Timeouts:** per command, for slow database restores.
- **Onboarding:** the `integrate-ultimate` skill gets a "Worktree setup" step. I read the project, write `.ultimate/worktree-setup.sh` and `-teardown.sh`, prove them in a scratch worktree and commit them. Postgres or anything with credentials becomes a question to you.
- **Databases, in the project's script:** SQLite is a copy-on-write clone of the source file, so it's near instant with no extra disk. Postgres is a `createdb -T` from a template, dropped on teardown.
- **For boxer:** copy the real `.env`, clone the 96 MB production SQLite file, and write `APP_URL`, `SERVER_PORT` and `VITE_PORT` from the worktree's port block.

**Easier alternative:** only the onboarding step, with no core change. It can already copy `.env` and the database using `ULTIMATE_SOURCE`, but dev servers still collide on :8000, and nothing cleans up databases or servers.

**Risks:** each worktree holds a copy of boxer's production data. Copy-on-write keeps disk flat and teardown deletes it, but a kept or dirty worktree keeps its copy.

**Decisions** (my picks: 1a 2a 3a 4a 5a, go):
1. **Scope:** (a) ports, environment, teardown, timeouts and the onboarding step; (b) onboarding step only; (c) (a) without teardown.
2. **Ports:** (a) a block of 10 per worktree; (b) a single `PORT`.
3. **Lander:** (a) `ULTIMATE_LANDER=1` so scripts skip the database there; (b) the lander runs the full script.
4. **Onboarding:** (a) a step in the skill, proven in a scratch worktree; (b) also a setup card.
5. **Boxer, once this lands:** (a) you tell boxer's @ultimate to read #226722 in the ultimate project (cross-project reads work) and set up its scripts; (b) you do it yourself.

Reply e.g. "1a 2a 3a 4a 5a, go".

**When agents pick up changed instructions** (#228203): an assessment; nothing is built yet.

**Mostly, it already works.** Agents don't need to "re-read": the new text simply replaces the old in their system prompt.
- **A project's `AGENTS.md`, `~/.ultimate/AGENTS.md`, and the list of skills:** rebuilt every turn, so the next turn sees the change.
- **@ultimate's and @sync's own instructions:** re-applied on every message they receive, so within minutes.
- **The lander:** re-applied on every landing.
- **Skill contents and `.ultimate/README.md`:** read from the file when used, so always current.
- **Ultimate's own `AGENTS.md`, in another project like boxer:** not in the prompt. Agents there are told to read it before changing Ultimate, so it's always current too.

**Two real gaps:**
1. **Nothing tells the agent that its instructions changed,** so it can keep acting on habits from the old text. The "Build changed" note only covers code, not `agents/`, `AGENTS.md` or skills.
2. **A coordinator that's already running keeps the instructions it started with,** even after `coordinator.md` changes. Workers and reviewers do too, but they're short-lived.

**Recommendation:** small, about +60 lines, extensions only, no restart.
- **A note:** the hidden note on the agent's next input gets a line like "Instructions changed: agents/ultimate.md, AGENTS.md. Your system prompt now has the new text; drop habits from the old one." It compares what that agent actually sees, so a branch is judged on its own worktree's files, and boxer isn't told about Ultimate's internal files. A conversation's first turn adds no note.
- **Coordinators follow their definition:** like standing agents, a running coordinator gets the current `coordinator.md` on each new input.
- **Cost:** standing agents already take one prompt-cache miss per instruction edit; the note adds none. Refreshing coordinators adds one miss per running coordinator, only when `coordinator.md` changes.

**Easier alternative:** add `agents/`, `AGENTS.md` and `skills/` to the existing build note. That's noisier: it would announce changes an agent never sees, e.g. `coordinator.md` in my conversation, or Ultimate's `AGENTS.md` in boxer.

Decisions (my picks: 1a 2a 3a, go):
1. **Scope:** (a) the note plus coordinator refresh; (b) the note only; (c) nothing, it mostly works already.
2. **What the note watches:** (a) agent instructions, the project's `AGENTS.md` files and the skill list; (b) agent instructions only.
3. **Branches:** (a) keep reading their own worktree's `AGENTS.md`, which updates when they merge main; (b) always read main's.

**A more detailed extension overview** (#230861): an assessment; nothing is built yet. It's small to medium, about +200 lines, with no restart if decision 3a works out.

**Inline expand rather than a modal.** Each row gets a chevron; clicking it opens the details right there, and the on/off toggle stays in the row. On a phone a modal would cover the list you're browsing, and with ~45 rows opening one at a time keeps your place. Details load only when you open a row.

For your `laravel` extension, the expanded row would show:
```
▾ laravel  this project · its folder                    [●]
  Laravel Boost MCP (php artisan boost:mcp) as one agent tool.
  TOOLS 1
   laravel   Call a Laravel Boost MCP tool (routes, schema…)
  PROVIDES — · NEEDS — · WANTS —
  ACTIONS — · DOCUMENTS — · EVENTS —
  PROMPT 1 section · 0 hooks
  ~/Projects/boxer/.ultimate/extensions/laravel
```
Empty groups fold into one dim line, and a busier one like `messages` lists its tool, actions, events and what it provides and needs.

**What it needs:**
- **Already in the browser:** tool names, actions, prompt sections, secrets, load errors, the README and the web parts (panels, slots, commands).
- **Missing:** tool descriptions, and what each extension provides, needs and wants. A small read-only action adds them.

**Easier alternative:** names only, with no new action, about 80 lines. It drops tool descriptions, which is the "what does this tool do" part you asked about, so I don't recommend it.

**Limits:**
- The panel shows the extensions of the instance it runs in, so boxer's appear only on boxer's own page.
- A switched-off extension shows "off: tools load when it's on".

**Decisions** (my picks: 1a 2a 3a 4a, go):
1. **Layout:** (a) inline expand; (b) a modal from an ⓘ button.
2. **Data:** (a) the new read-only action, with tool descriptions and provides/needs/wants; (b) names only.
3. **Tool descriptions:** (a) read them without touching core, if possible; (b) a one-line core change that needs a restart.
4. **Full contract text** (`api.ts`/`refs.ts`) in the row: (a) no, the summary and counts are enough; (b) a "show contract" fold.

It's UI, so you'll get a preview before it lands. Reply e.g. "1a 2a 3a 4a, go".

**The transcript losing the bottom after you send** (#230946): an assessment; nothing is built yet.

**Yesterday's fix works:** sending from a scrolled-up position, from the bottom, at phone width, and with late codemode summary lines all stayed pinned on a test instance.

**The cause of what you still see** is the browser's own scroll anchoring. When a row above the view shrinks while the last row grows in the same moment, Chrome moves the scroll position up to keep the shrinking row on screen. The scroll library we use (`use-stick-to-bottom`) can't tell that from you scrolling up, so it stops following until you scroll down or send again. Real runs do exactly this often:
- a codemode summary line replaces a longer raw header;
- "working · N steps" folds into its list as the next row arrives;
- the "working…" line disappears as the answer appears;
- a triage verdict or a divider swaps in.

On the test instance, forcing that change un-stuck the view by 150 px, and later growth wasn't followed. With anchoring off, it stayed at the bottom.

There's a smaller second trigger: loading older history mid-run can switch following off while the smooth scroll is still catching up.

**Caveat:** this was reproduced by forcing the layout shift on a test instance. Your real conversation was idle, so no live failure was captured.

**Fix:** small, about 10 lines in `web/src/app/transcript.tsx`.
- Turn anchoring off only while the view follows the bottom. When you've scrolled up to read, anchoring stays on, so a summary changing above you doesn't move your text.
- Stop following on a history load only when you've actually left the bottom.
- Same library, nothing new installed.
